## EDA insights
1. Weekly_Sales is strongly right-skewed (skewness 3.26; mean $15,981 vs median $7,612). A small number of very large values dominate squared-error metrics such as RMSE.
2. Holiday weeks average $17,036 per record vs $15,901 for regular weeks (+7.1%), but the labeled data contains only 10 distinct holiday weeks, so this effect rests on few events.
3. Strong seasonality: month 12 has the highest average weekly sales ($19,356) and month 1 the lowest ($14,126); this pattern is consistent with seasonal demand, although the data cannot confirm the cause.
4. Store type matters: average weekly sales per record are Type A $20,100, Type B $12,237, Type C $9,520; store Size correlates with sales (r = 0.24).
5. Sales are concentrated: the top 5 departments (92, 95, 38, 72, 90) account for 28.5% of all recorded sales, so department identity is a major driver.

## Outlier investigation
- IQR bounds: -25,110 to 47,395; 35,521 of 421,570 rows (8.4%) are flagged, all above the upper bound (0 below the lower bound).
- Holiday-week share: 7.4% of outliers vs 7.0% of all rows.
- Nov-Dec share: 15.7% of outliers vs 12.7% of all rows.
- 93.8% of outlier rows belong to a Store/Dept/ISO-week combination that is an outlier in at least 2 different years (recurring seasonal peaks, not one-off glitches).
- Top departments among outliers (dept: count): 38: 4,348, 95: 4,242, 92: 4,102, 90: 2,832, 40: 2,797 (these 5 departments hold 51.6% of all outliers).
- Negative Weekly_Sales rows (likely returns/adjustments): 1,285. They are kept because they are real recorded values and cannot be verified as errors.
- DECISION: outliers are NOT removed. Evidence: they are concentrated in a few high-volume departments, they recur for the same Store/Dept/week in different years, and they are only mildly over-represented in holiday and Nov-Dec weeks. That pattern points to structurally large departments and repeating seasonal peaks rather than one-off data errors. It does not prove that every single value is correct. Removing them would teach the model to under-predict the largest sales, and tree-based models split on thresholds instead of fitting one global line, so extreme values distort them less than a linear fit.

## CPI / Unemployment availability audit (UNRESOLVED)
- features.csv has CPI/Unemployment values up to 2013-04-26; 33.2% of test.csv rows (later weeks) have none.
- CPI differs across stores at the same date (median 15 distinct values across stores per week), so it is not a single national series.
- Within one store and calendar month CPI takes a median of 4 distinct value(s) across 39 months per store, so it changes gradually week to week.
- The dataset has NO publication/release timestamps. Whether the CPI and Unemployment value attached to a week was actually known BEFORE that week begins CANNOT be verified from these files. Official macro statistics are typically published after the period they describe, so the value shown for a week may be later information than a true pre-week forecast would have. STATUS: UNRESOLVED. The features are kept (project decision) but flagged.
- Ablation (Random Forest (tuned), same CV folds): CV MAE 2,822.41 with CPI+Unemployment vs 2,662.38 without them (-5.7%).
